1.explanation:
1. cascader-select/__docs__/index.md & index.en-us.md: Provide the component’s API, configuration options (including virtual scroll usage), and default styling notes.
2. cascader-select/scss/: Contains the Sass styles that set background colors for the dropdown panels and list items; we need to verify the CSS selectors that apply when items are recycled by the virtual list.
3. cascader-select/theme/index.jsx: Exposes theme tokens (background colors, panel styles) used at runtime; ensures that the overlay’s background is applied consistently.
4. virtual-list/index.jsx & style.js: Show how the virtualized list is implemented (node recycling, container wrappers, style injections) and how backgrounds might be inherited or lost when items are re-rendered, which is at the heart of the visual glitch when scrolling.
1.bug_scenario:
In the screenshot the CascaderSelect dropdown is opened with virtual scrolling enabled. As you scroll through the long list of items, you can see that the background panels (the cascading columns) are rendering with inconsistent background colors – some rows or sections appear transparent or show the wrong shade. The menu columns (each cascader level) should have a solid white (or theme‐controlled) background, but when virtual scrolling recycles DOM nodes you can observe “holes” or mismatched background stripes behind list items.

Key on‐screen elements involved:
- The CascaderSelect trigger button and input placeholder (“请选择”) at top
- Three cascading panels (left = provinces, mid = cities, right = counties)
- Virtual‐scrolled list items within each panel (only the visible subset is rendered)
- The overlay panel container background and individual item backgrounds
- Scrollbars and recycled DOM nodes causing background inconsistencies
